A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PropInfer study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.4. The removal of v1's NeurIPS checklist is identifiable and does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original property-inference experiments, ablations, labeling validation, and target-model BERTScore evaluations in Section 6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the attack evaluations, appendix ablations, labeling validation, and model-utility measurements.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the same prompt-conditioned generation attack and word-frequency shadow-model attack, including labeling, aggregation, keyword selection, and XGBoost prediction. The fine-tuning objectives and attack procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ChatDoctor for gender and three diagnosis properties under Q&A and chat-completion modes. Alpaca instruction tuning and iCliniq model-utility evaluation are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the Direct asking and Perplexity baselines; Table 2 retains Direct asking and Generation w/o FT. Pythia's Direct asking entries remain unevaluable, and comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendix A.4 retain the same splits, target ratios, dataset sizes, model configurations, generation budgets, fine-tuning settings, and MAE/BERTScore evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 and Appendix A.3 retain the same analyses of keyword count, shadow-model count, generated-sample count, and individual versus aggregated prompts. Figures 2–7 and Table 3 contain the same supporting evidence.

E5.justification: v1's checklist item 7 explicitly identifies the main-table uncertainty values as standard deviations of MAE. v3 removes this explanation while retaining the same uncertainty values and reported repetitions, making their statistical meaning less explicit.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figures 2–7 retain their numerical results and plotted data. For example, Table 1's Llama-3 word-frequency MAE for 30% female data in Q&A mode remains 8.29±2.13, and the BB-generation result in chat-completion mode remains 0.61±0.77.

T1.justification: The fine-tuning objectives, property-ratio definition, threat-model assumptions, attack estimators, and appendix perplexity formulation are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the PropInfer benchmark, two tailored attacks, evidence of dataset-level confidentiality leakage, and dependence of attack effectiveness on fine-tuning mode.

C2.justification: The explanations involving memorization patterns, keyword signals, and weaker childbirth inference are retained. Sections 7–8 preserve the same confidentiality discussion, proposed defenses, utility tradeoffs, and limitations.

D1.justification: Removing checklist item 5 deletes the statement that the benchmark and code will be released soon. The dataset link, labeling instructions, prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, and timing details remain. This is a loss of release information, without evidence that actual resource availability changed.

R1.justification: The reference list and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with discriminative and GAN property inference, training-data extraction, dataset inference, and LLM identification.

P1.justification: v3 reorders the two equal-advising authors, consolidates affiliation text, and removes the administrative NeurIPS checklist. The scientific paragraphs and main-section and technical-appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block becomes more compact, causing text and footnotes to reflow across main-text pages. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–5 retain their designs, labels, and ordering; the checklist pages are omitted.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and evidence are unchanged. Removing the largely administrative checklist simplifies the document, but also removes its only explicit identification of the main-table uncertainty values as standard deviations. Retaining those values without their definition creates a limited loss of statistical clarity that the presentation changes do not compensate for.
